instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Here We Go Again
cards.instruction: Use every new disagreement to prove the same relationship pattern is repeating, then raise the consequences.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I taught you to call when you're late. Another dinner kept warm until eleven. Are we starting that lesson again?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: This time my battery died.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Last time it was the train. You remember the excuses beautifully. Tomorrow I eat at seven; you can practise arriving.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll borrow a phone next time. Please keep a plate for me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Still expecting your teacher to do the caring part. Miss another call and you'll use those cooking lessons too. Buy your own ingredients.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Sunday cancelled again? I taught you to let Mum know before she makes up the spare bed.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Work changed my shift. I can't help it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Last time it was overtime. You're very good at explaining things to me. Now graduate to telling her yourself.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She'll think I don't want to visit. Could you soften it?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Back to the first lesson: you cancel, I apologise. You'll arrange the next visit with her too. Let's see if any of my teaching stuck.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Let Me Lean
cards.instruction: Get someone to carry part of the emotional burden without making you name how heavy it has become.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could you cancel our anniversary table? Restaurant number's on the fridge. Use that calm telephone voice we practised.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: What's happened?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: One question at a time. First get them on the phone for me. You used to need me beside you for this.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll call. They might ask whether you want another date.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Say no. Firmly, without filling the silence. I'll put the anniversary glasses away while you talk. Don't go as soon as you hang up.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Read the first line of this letter before I do. Slowly. You always rushed when I was teaching you.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Shall I read it aloud?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Only if you can keep your face ordinary. You're better at that now. Mine won't be much help.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll sit beside you. We can take one line at a time.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. Keep your finger under the words, like we used to. I'll follow it. Don't move on until I have.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Stay Until I’m Steady
cards.instruction: Keep someone present until you feel steady enough to face what comes next without them.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Stay for tea. I need to tell the children about tomorrow's operation. You remember how often I made you rehearse before facing an audience.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We've had three cups.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then be my audience. Don't prompt if I stop; you always wanted the next word too quickly.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: My taxi's outside.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Ask for two minutes. Let me get through 'I'll be in hospital' once without a prompt. Then I'll fetch them.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before you leave me in this new flat, count five breaths with me. Slowly, the way I showed you before your exams.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That was five. Shall I close the door?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Not yet. You still race the last one. Count again while I look at the empty kitchen.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll wait here while you put the kettle on.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good, you've learned not to hurry someone. Stay until it boils. Then I'll try pouring one cup without getting yours out.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Understand the Hurt
cards.instruction: Make someone acknowledge why their action hurt, not merely agree that it happened.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You remember how I made you pick one friendly face before a concert? I saved you the front-row seat at mine.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I told you work might run late.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes. You've learned to give a warning. But I looked at that empty chair before every song. Tell me what I was looking for.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Someone who knew what getting through those songs meant to you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's it. You used to tell me any friendly face would do. Do you understand now why I couldn't just choose another one?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I used to make you repeat what you'd heard before you answered. I texted 'I've lost my job.' You replied, 'What's for dinner?'

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I thought something normal would help.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You skipped the listening part. Can you see why I felt like your cook?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I meant we could go out. I'll book somewhere.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Wait. You've always wanted to move on before we'd finished this part. Tell me why that message sounded like another job for me. Then we can book.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Tell Me I Did Enough
cards.instruction: Get someone to reassure you that your effort, choice, or survival was enough.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I stayed through the whole speech. You used to bring your shaking notes to me afterwards. Was that enough?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You forgot a paragraph.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Mark the thing I asked about. How often did I tell you that? I stayed at the microphone.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You did. I'll help you practise the missing bit tomorrow.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're very thorough now. Could you give your old teacher a pass instead? Tell me I've earned tomorrow off.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: One painting. That's all I finished for our exhibition. You're usually the one asking me if you've done enough.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll spread mine out. Nobody will notice the gap.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: No, keep the spacing we practised. Don't rearrange your work to disguise mine. Tell me whether this one deserves to be here.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It belongs in the middle. It's the one people will see first.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good eye. Will you introduce me as the other painter, then? I'd like to hear my best pupil say that.
